items.title: Vanishing of H^1 of a curve fibre follows from global R^1 vanishing, or after any base change hitting the point
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a proper morphism f : X -> Y and a point y with dim X_y <= 1, the lemma shows H^1(X_y, O_{X_y}) = 0 if either R^1 f_* O_X = 0, or more generally if some base change g : Y' -> Y with y in the image kills R^1 of the pulled-back structure pushforward. The retained proof is written: shrink Y around y so all fibres have dimension <= 1 (Limits, lemma proper-top-cohomology... cited via the openness-of-bounded-fibre-dimension result Morphisms, lemma openness-bounded-dimension-fibres), note Y affine; then R^1 f_* O_X is a finite type quasi-coherent module whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change (the two cited Limits lemmas: finite type plus vanishing above the fibre dimension), so the fibre cohomology is the fibre of the sheaf, and the vanishing after base change through g with y in the image forces the stalk at y to vanish; the lemma follows immediately from these named inputs. Retained author proof at lines 20930-20940.
